channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Central Asia and Caucasus Face Growing Water Security Challenges, ADB Analysis Warns
item.description: An Asian Development Bank analysis highlights accelerating glacier melt in Central Asia and the Caucasus, warning of increased risks of drought, landslides, and glacial lake outburst floods. Average temperatures could rise by up to 5°C by 2085, impacting water availability and storage.

item.title: Turkmenistan Poised to Complete Section of TAPI Pipeline by End of 2026
item.description: Turkmenistan aims to complete a section of the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) pipeline by the end of 2026, stretching from the Turkmen border to Herat, Afghanistan. Approximately 80% of the route is prepared, with welding and hydrostatic testing underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Three Nuclear Power Plants, Secures Uranium Reserves for 100 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to build three nuclear power plants to meet growing electricity demands and establish a nuclear industry cluster. The country, second globally in uranium reserves and a major producer, views uranium as a strategic resource for energy and economic development. Plans also include training specialists and developing nuclear technologies for medicine and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Maintain Key Tax Rates Unchanged Through 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to keep its main tax rates unchanged through 2027. The state budget for the upcoming year is projected to have revenues of 416 trillion soums and expenditures of 464 trillion soums. The inflation target is set at no more than 6%.

item.title: Uzbekistan Economy Projected to Grow 7% to $232 Billion by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's economy is expected to grow by 7% in 2027, reaching $232 billion, according to a meeting on state budget targets and macroeconomic forecasts. The current year's growth is projected at a minimum of 8%, with GDP exceeding $200 million. By 2030, the goal is to reach $300 billion, and by 2036, $10,000 per capita.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Development Model Prioritizes Environmental Security
item.description: Uzbekistan is integrating environmental security into its development model, balancing economic growth with ecological sustainability. President Mirziyoyev's initiatives at COP31 highlight a commitment to protecting national interests and Central Asian regional well-being amidst global climate challenges like extreme heat and water scarcity. The 'Adolat' party also recognizes the right to a healthy environment.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Orders Review of Cases Affecting Innocent Businesspeople
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered a review of cases where innocent businesspeople were allegedly harmed during anti-organized crime operations. He acknowledged that some individuals, possibly 10-15%, were wrongly implicated. The president's directive came after a resident complained about her husband being entrapped and pressured to forfeit property.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Halt Operations at Some Uranium Fields for Strategic Reserve
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create a strategic reserve of uranium to meet domestic needs, temporarily suspending operations at certain fields. The Atomic Energy Agency stated this is linked to developing nuclear energy and rising global demand. Some finished uranium products will also be stored, with reserves established at each nuclear power plant for continuous operation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Warns Against Attempts to Destabilize Country Ahead of Elections
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov warned against political forces attempting to disrupt stability and prevent upcoming elections. He specifically mentioned a plot to incite ethnic Uzbek-Kyrgyz conflict to postpone the vote. Japarov assured that law enforcement has the capacity to maintain order and called for unity among all citizens living in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Allocates Over 175 Trillion Sums to Education and Healthcare in 2027 Budget
item.description: Uzbekistan's 2027 state budget projects expenditures of 464 trillion sums and revenues of 416 trillion sums. Approximately 175.7 trillion sums are earmarked for education and healthcare reforms. Education will receive 114.3 trillion sums, an increase of 14 trillion, while healthcare funding will rise by 12 trillion to 61.4 trillion sums.

item.title: Afghanistan to Export 100,000 Tons of Potatoes to Uzbekistan
item.description: Afghanistan will export 100,000 tons of potatoes to Uzbekistan. The first batch, consisting of eight trucks, has already departed for Termiz via the Hairatan port. This agreement was reached between the Chambers of Commerce and Industry of both nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims for $232 Billion GDP by 2027, Eyes $300 Billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reach a GDP of $232 billion by 2027 and $300 billion by 2030, according to President Mirziyoyev's economic development meeting. The country aims to attract $65 billion in foreign investment and achieve an annual economic growth of at least 7% from 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan Wins Five-Year International Investment Arbitration Case Against Turkish Claimants
item.description: Uzbekistan has secured a victory in an international investment arbitration case initiated by a group of Turkish citizens. The tribunal fully rejected all claims against the state, concluding a five-year dispute.

item.title: Suspect arrested in Kokshetau for defrauding individuals in car auction scheme
item.description: A 40-year-old man has been arrested in Kokshetau on suspicion of defrauding five people in a car auction scheme. He allegedly promised to help them buy cars at a lower price, taking over 41 million tenge in total. The victims did not receive the cars or their money back, and the suspect is now in custody.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice reports on budget spending and performance indicators
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice presented information on budget spending for 2026, focusing on strategic goals and performance. The ministry utilized 85% of allocated funds, exceeding targets for most indicators. However, one indicator's performance was below 50%. The review highlighted the need for legislative proposals to simplify public services.

item.title: Kazakhstan University Discusses President's Address on New National Priorities
item.description: Scholars, lawyers, and students at Zhasulan Tashenev University held a discussion on the President's address, "Kazakhstan's Current Tasks at a New Historical Stage." The meeting analyzed presidential initiatives and their impact on socio-economic and political life, seeking new directions for science and higher education.

item.title: Uzbekistan Advances Climate Resilience with Green Technology and Resource Management Initiatives
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing reforms based on 'green' technologies and rational resource management to combat climate change. The country has met its goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP by 35% and aims to cut harmful emissions by 50% by 2035, prioritizing green energy generation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Criticizes Transport Sector, Demands Improvements in Transit Potential
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev chaired an emergency Security Council meeting on the transport sector, criticizing its current state and demanding improvements. He emphasized the need for Kazakhstan to proactively engage in international transport structures and enhance transit capabilities for competitiveness.

item.title: Kazakh President Meets with National Security Committee Head
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Ермек Сагимбаев, Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB). Сагимбаев reported on the committee's activities, including counter-terrorism, extremism, organized crime, drug trafficking, anti-corruption, and cybersecurity efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Customs Lacks Capability to Detect Fake IMEI Codes
item.description: Uzbekistan's customs authorities do not possess the technical means to identify counterfeit IMEI codes on mobile phones, stated Farhod Olimjonov of the Customs Committee. Detecting such falsifications requires specialized knowledge beyond the customs' current systems. The committee is collaborating with relevant agencies to address this issue.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Dialogue Highlights Business and Human Rights Risks
item.description: Tashkent hosted the first National Dialogue on Business and Human Rights, organized by the UNDP and the National Center for Human Rights. The event presented findings on national baseline assessments, identifying 12 key human rights issues in business, including informal employment and labor protection.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Enhanced CIS Cooperation in Emergency Prevention
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Emergency Situations proposed strengthening cooperation among CIS rescue agencies at the 38th Interstate Council meeting in Shymkent. Minister Azizbek Ikramov highlighted reforms shifting focus from response to prevention and risk identification, alongside modernization efforts.

item.title: Rosatom Highlights Benefits of Nuclear Power Plants for Host Countries
item.description: Rosatom stated that local companies can perform up to 30% of work during NPP construction, and electricity tariffs are predictable for decades. First Deputy CEO Kirill Komarov noted that nuclear fuel costs are a small fraction of electricity prices, making them less volatile than gas or coal.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pitches $15 Billion in Infrastructure Projects to European Investors
item.description: Uzbekistan presented seven infrastructure projects totaling over $15 billion to European investors in Paris during the Paris InfraWeek 2026 forum. Key areas include toll roads, airport development, and railway networks, with discussions held with major financial institutions.

item.title: Former Staff of Atbasar Prison Sentenced in Torture Case
item.description: A court in the Atbasar district of Akmola region has sentenced 12 former employees of the Atbasar prison accused of cruelty towards inmates. The sentences range from restricted liberty to probation, with some released due to time served. All convicted individuals lost their special military ranks and were banned from law enforcement work for three years.

item.title: Tokayev Criticizes Kazakhstan Railways, Outlines Transit Goals
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has demanded Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) improve profitability and streamline operations, urging the removal of obstacles causing cargo delays. Speaking at a Security Council meeting on transport and transit development in Astana, he emphasized Kazakhstan's strategic location and the need to enhance transit routes, including air and sea transport, and improve border and customs efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Chairs Security Council Meeting on Transport Development
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev chaired an urgent Security Council meeting focused on developing the transport and transit sector. Discussions covered international transport corridors, strengthening transit potential, and improving logistics. The President criticized the current situation and emphasized the need for proactive engagement in global transport architecture.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Receives Report from National Security Committee
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB), Yermek Sagimbayev. The President was briefed on the committee's performance this year and its tasks for the upcoming period. Discussions included combating terrorism, extremism, organized crime, drug trafficking, corruption, and ensuring cybersecurity.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Criticizes National Railway Company's Performance
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sharply criticized the performance of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) during a Security Council meeting on transport and transit development. He emphasized the need for Kazakhstan to adopt a proactive stance in the global transport architecture, highlighting that competitiveness depends on speed, predictability, attractive tariffs, and reliability.

item.title: Two Fake Real Estate Agents Arrested in Tashkent for Rental Scams
item.description: Two individuals have been apprehended in Tashkent's Bektemir district on suspicion of fraud related to renting out properties. The suspects allegedly posted ads for cheap rentals, took advance payments, and then cut off contact, defrauding over ten people. Police seized phones, SIM cards, and bank cards.

item.title: Uzbekistan Wins 5-Year International Arbitration Case Against Turkish Claimants
item.description: Uzbekistan has emerged victorious in a five-year international arbitration case against Turkish claimants, including Mehmet Zeki Obuz. All claims made by the Turkish citizens regarding a food industry enterprise have been rejected by the tribunal. The dispute involved a company in the food sector.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizens in Russia Urged to Carefully Check Labor Contracts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs advises its citizens in Russia to strictly adhere to migration laws and thoroughly review all labor contracts before signing. Citizens are encouraged to verify employer information, clearly understand contract terms, working hours, and location, and be wary of high salary offers in conflict zones.

item.title: Twenty Chinese Citizens Arrested for Working Illegally in a Kazakh Village
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region arrested 20 Chinese citizens working in a village. Their visas indicated they were supposed to work in Almaty, but they lacked local work permits. The court found them guilty and sentenced each to one day of administrative arrest.

item.title: Muruntau: Inside the World's Largest Gold Mine
item.description: Muruntau, Uzbekistan, is the world's largest gold mine by production volume. Operating 24/7, it yields 60-80 tons of gold annually, about 5% of global output. The gold particles are microscopic, requiring massive ore processing. Ore is blasted, transported by trucks, and lifted via a unique conveyor system.

item.title: Russia Dismisses UN Report on Afghan Opium as 'Political Propaganda'
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry has labeled a UN report on Afghan opiates as 'tailor-made political propaganda,' stating it hinders efforts to combat drug trafficking. The ministry criticized the UNODC report for being unbalanced and relying on indirect evidence, despite acknowledging Afghanistan's ongoing drug problem and security forces' operations.

item.title: Former Ukrainian PM's Spokesperson Injured in Moscow Car Bombing
item.description: Serhiy Zavorotny, spokesperson for former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, was injured in a car bombing in Moscow. The explosion occurred while Zavorotny was driving in the Chertanovo district. This is the second car bombing in Russia in two days. Zavorotny sustained severe injuries, including the amputation of his left hand.

item.title: Twenty Chinese Citizens Detained in Kazakhstan for Working Without Permits
item.description: A court in the Zhelezinsky district of Pavlodar region has ordered the arrest of twenty Chinese citizens. They were found working in the village of Urlyutobe in October 2026 without the necessary permits. The individuals admitted guilt, acknowledging the circumstances of their administrative offense. Each was sentenced to one day of administrative arrest.

item.title: Tashkent: Prevention Inspector Detained Amidst Conflict Between Police and Bailiffs
item.description: A prevention inspector from the Yangikhyot district police department has been detained in Tashkent following a conflict with state bailiffs. The incident occurred when bailiffs attempted to collect a debt, and police officers allegedly used physical force, causing minor injuries and preventing the debt collection. The police allegedly held the bailiffs against their will.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Adds 66,000 Companies to Forced Liquidation List
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service has initiated the third phase of forced liquidation for inactive legal entities and cancellation of tax registration for individual entrepreneurs. The new list includes 66,000 taxpayers, comprising 15,600 legal entities and 50,400 individual entrepreneurs. Companies can avoid liquidation by fulfilling tax obligations within 30 days.

item.title: Thousands of Gas Cylinders Illegally Stored Found in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan has uncovered cases of illegal storage of thousands of gas cylinders intended for resale at commercial prices. On November 9 alone, seven instances involving 249 cylinders were found. Violators include employees of gas supply organizations. Authorities urge citizens to report suspicious trade and illegal storage of gas cylinders.
